numberOfTests.description: the number of test vectors in this test

HpkeTestGroup.description: HPKE single-shot decryption (Open) in base mode (RFC 9180). Each group fixes one (KEM, KDF, AEAD) ciphersuite. Given the recipient private key skRm, info, aad, enc, and ct, the implementation runs SetupBaseR followed by Open and MUST recover pt for valid cases or fail for invalid cases. Acceptable cases are interoperability probes that an implementation following RFC 9180 literally accepts; an implementation may reject them, but if it accepts one it MUST produce exactly the given output. The primary direction tested is SetupBaseR + Open; cases with ikmE additionally pin the sender direction (see doc/hpke.md).

type.description: A legacy field, test files contain only one type per file

kemId.description: The two-byte HPKE KEM identifier from the IANA HPKE KEM registry (RFC 9180, extended by draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05)

kdfId.description: The two-byte HPKE KDF identifier (RFC 9180 Table 3)

aeadId.description: The two-byte HPKE AEAD identifier (RFC 9180 Table 5)

comment.description: A brief description of the test case

skRm.description: The serialized recipient private key (SerializePrivateKey of skR). For ML-KEM KEMs this is the 64-byte d || z seed; for DHKEM(X25519) it is the 32-byte unclamped scalar (see skEm).

pkRm.description: The serialized recipient public key (SerializePublicKey of pkR), derivable from skRm and provided for convenience

ikmE.description: Optional. The 32-byte randomness input to deterministic encapsulation (ikmE in the RFC 9180 Appendix A test vectors; the input to EncapDerand in draft-ietf-hpke-hpke-05 Appendix C.1). For DHKEM(X25519) it is the DeriveKeyPair input for the sender's ephemeral key pair, (skE, pkE) = DeriveKeyPair(ikmE); for ML-KEM (draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05) it is the randomness m passed to FIPS 203 ML-KEM.Encaps_internal. When present, deterministic encapsulation reproduces enc and ct exactly, so an implementation with such a hook can also check the sender direction. Present for honestly sealed valid and acceptable cases. Omitted for invalid cases (enc or ct is mutated or forged), for the valid ML-KEM ImplicitRejection, Strcmp, and MalleableCiphertext cases (ct is sealed under the implicit-rejection secret K-bar = J(z || enc), which no encapsulation produces), and for acceptable cases whose enc an honest sender does not produce.

skEm.description: Optional, DHKEM only. The sender's ephemeral private key skEm = SerializePrivateKey(skE), where (skE, pkE) = DeriveKeyPair(ikmE) and SerializePrivateKey is the identity for X25519 (draft-ietf-hpke-hpke-05 Section 7.1.2). Provided for deterministic-encapsulation test hooks that take the raw ephemeral private key rather than ikmE. Present exactly when ikmE is present for a DHKEM; absent for ML-KEM, which has no ephemeral key pair. For X25519 this is the unclamped 32-byte string that DeriveKeyPair returns, matching the RFC 9180 Appendix A test vectors. The text of RFC 9180 Section 7.1.2 requires SerializePrivateKey to clamp, so an implementation that follows it (e.g. Go crypto/hpke PrivateKey.Bytes) re-serializes the key to different bytes; compare public keys or results, not re-serialized private keys. X25519 treats clamped and unclamped scalars identically (RFC 7748 Section 5); an API that requires a clamped scalar needs the key clamped before import. See doc/hpke.md.

info.description: The HPKE info string bound into the key schedule

aad.description: The additional authenticated data passed to the AEAD Open

enc.description: The KEM encapsulated key (Nenc bytes) consumed by SetupBaseR

ct.description: The AEAD sealed message (ciphertext || tag) produced by ContextS.Seal

pt.description: The expected recovered plaintext for valid and acceptable cases; empty for invalid cases
